facts.title: The Moon is slowly moving away
facts.fact: The Moon drifts about 3.8 centimeters farther from Earth each year.

facts.title: Octopuses have distributed intelligence
facts.fact: A large part of an octopus nervous system is in its arms, helping each arm sense and react.

facts.title: Ancient concrete still survives
facts.fact: Some Roman concrete structures have lasted for nearly two thousand years in harsh sea conditions.

facts.title: Your brain edits reality
facts.fact: The brain fills blind spots and smooths motion so your experience feels continuous.

facts.title: Neutron stars are unbelievably dense
facts.fact: A teaspoon of neutron-star material would have a mass of billions of tons on Earth.

facts.title: Trees can share signals underground
facts.fact: Many forests use root and fungal networks to exchange chemical signals and nutrients.

factImages.title: Earth has a hidden inner core
factImages.fact: Earth's solid inner core sits inside a liquid outer core, helping power the planet's magnetic field.

factImages.title: The Milky Way is on the move
factImages.fact: Our galaxy is traveling through space and will eventually merge with the Andromeda galaxy.

factImages.title: Honey never truly expires
factImages.fact: Properly sealed honey can remain edible for thousands of years because of its low moisture and acidity.

factImages.title: Lightning is hotter than the Sun's surface
factImages.fact: A lightning bolt can heat the surrounding air to temperatures far above the Sun's visible surface.

factImages.title: The pyramids were once bright white
factImages.fact: The Great Pyramid was originally covered in polished limestone casing stones that reflected sunlight.

factImages.title: The first computer bug was literal
factImages.fact: Engineers once recorded an actual moth found inside a computer relay as a bug in the system.

factImages.title: Memories change when recalled
factImages.fact: Every time a memory is remembered, the brain can slightly rewrite or reshape it.

factImages.title: Your brain predicts before you notice
factImages.fact: The brain constantly predicts incoming information, helping you react quickly to the world.

factImages.title: Black holes bend light
factImages.fact: A black hole's gravity is so strong that it can curve the path of light around it.

factImages.title: Mars has the tallest volcano
factImages.fact: Olympus Mons on Mars is the tallest known volcano in the solar system.

factImages.title: Some plants can move quickly
factImages.fact: The Venus flytrap snaps shut when tiny trigger hairs are touched twice.

factImages.title: The ocean is mostly unexplored
factImages.fact: Much of Earth's deep ocean remains unmapped and unseen by humans.

factImages.title: Ancient libraries shaped civilizations
factImages.fact: Libraries preserved knowledge, maps, astronomy, medicine, and laws across generations.

factImages.title: Stonehenge tracks the Sun
factImages.fact: Stonehenge aligns with sunrise and sunset positions during solstices.

factImages.title: Dreams can train emotions
factImages.fact: Dreaming may help the brain process memories, stress, and emotional experiences.

factImages.title: Attention can hide obvious things
factImages.fact: When focus is narrow, people can miss large changes happening in plain sight.
